source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in CKD (2024 Update)
excerpt: In patients receiving an ACEi or ARB who develop serum potassium > 5.5 mmol/L, evaluate for reversible causes (diet, supplements, hemolysis), obtain a 12-lead ECG, and temporarily reduce or hold the RAAS inhibitor until potassium normalizes.

source: ACC/AHA Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure
excerpt: A serum creatinine increase of up to 30% above baseline after initiating or titrating an ACE inhibitor is expected and acceptable; increases > 30% or acute elevation without a known baseline warrant evaluation for acute kidney injury, volume depletion, or bilateral renal artery stenosis.

source: European Resuscitation Council / Clinical Chemistry Standards
excerpt: Elevated serum potassium (> 5.5 mmol/L) in an asymptomatic patient without ECG changes should be verified for pre-analytical artifact (specimen hemolysis, prolonged tourniquet application, or delayed centrifugation) before initiating aggressive potassium-lowering therapy.

topic: Lisinopril FDA Prescribing Information — Renal & Electrolyte Warnings
source: FDA Drug Label: Lisinopril Oral Tablets (DailyMed)
excerpt: Monitor serum potassium and renal function periodically in patients receiving Lisinopril. Risk factors for hyperkalemia include renal insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, and concomitant use of potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements.
